dialog.body: Good morning, Newport Recreation, this is Beth. How can I help you?
Hi, good morning. Um, my name is Neusa Fortes. I'm calling for my mother. She is... [pause] interested in a class. A class at the, the recreation center, I think.
Sure, happy to help. Do you know which class she's looking at? We've got fitness, art, a few things for older adults, and lots for kids too.

Okay, so, she saw something. A flyer. At the library, I believe. It said, um, something about a watercolor, or maybe it was pottery. I'm sorry, I'm in the middle of a jigsaw puzzle right now, and there is one piece, one piece, missing, so my head is a little bit, um, elsewhere.
Oh no, the missing piece! It's always under the couch or in the box lid. Don't worry, take your time. Watercolor and pottery are both ones we run, so we can sort it out.

Thank you. Okay. So. My mother, she does not have a lot of money. Fixed income. And the flyer, I think, said there was a scholarship. A scholarship for the class fees. Is that, is that a real thing? Or did I read it wrong?

No, you read it right. We do have financial assistance for program fees. It's an application, and it's based on household income. Usually you fill out a short form and bring or send something to show your situation.
A form. Okay. And is it a scholarship, or is it, like, a discount? Because I thought scholarship meant, um, you win it. Like a competition.
No competition. People call it a scholarship, but it's really help paying for the class. If you qualify, it takes some or all of the fee off.
Some or all. Okay. And, um, who fills it out? Me, or my mother? Because it's her class, but I am the one, the one, who is calling.
Best if your mom signs it since she's the participant. But you can absolutely help her fill it out. A lot of families do it together.

Okay, good. That is good. Now, the other thing. Is there an age limit? Because she is, um, she is over sixty-five. I don't know if the class is for, for young people. Or maybe it is only for adults, under, like, sixty-five?

Good question. Most of our adult classes don't have an upper age limit at all. Some of the kids' programs have age ranges, but watercolor and pottery for adults are open to grown-ups of any age. The flyer might list a minimum, like eighteen and up.
Eighteen and up. Okay. So there is a minimum, but not a maximum. Is that right? I want to say it right to her.
That's right. Minimum for some, no maximum for the adult ones.
Okay. But then, the scholarship. Does the scholarship have an age limit? Like, you have to be a senior, or you have to be a child? I read something that said, um, youth. Youth scholarship.

Ah, I see where the mix-up could be. We have assistance for youth programs, and there's help for adults as well. I'd want to double check which form applies to your mom's class. Let me look at what's on my screen. Can you hold a sec?
Yes. Yes, I can hold.
Thanks for waiting. Okay, so the assistance application is the same basic form, and it asks for the program name and the participant's age. It isn't limited to kids. Income is what matters.
So it is not just for youth. Okay. I was, I was wrong about that. Sorry. And where do I get the form? Is it online, or do I come in?
Both. You can pick one up at the front desk here, or find it on the city's recreation page. Or I can have one mailed to your mom if you give me an address.
Um, no, no address on the phone, please. I will, I will just come in. What are the hours? Today is Friday, right?
Yes, Friday. We're open till late afternoon today. If you come by this afternoon, the front desk will have the forms. Otherwise Monday works too.
This afternoon, okay. So I bring the form, and she signs, and then, wait. Does she pay first, and then they give the money back? Or does she not pay at all?
You'd submit the application first. Once it's approved, the fee gets adjusted before she pays. So she shouldn't have to pay and wait for a refund.
Okay. Approved, then adjusted, then pay. Did I say that right?
You did. Approved, adjusted, then pay whatever's left, if anything.
And, um, how long does approved take? Because the class, I think, starts soon. I am not sure when.

Usually it's a few days, but I'd turn it in as early as you can. And the class start date will be right on the flyer or the schedule. If you tell me whether it's watercolor or pottery, I can check the dates for you.
Oh. I don't know which. I will ask her. It was one, one, of those. I will call back, or I will see you at the desk and ask there.
Either works. And if you leave a number, I can call you once I've looked it up.
Okay. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-six-one.
Got it, four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-six-one. And that's Neusa?
Yes. N-E-U-S-A. Fortes. Thank you, Beth. I think I understand. Mostly. Form, signature, approved, adjusted. And no maximum age.
Perfect summary. Good luck with that last puzzle piece!
Thank you. I will check the couch. Goodbye.
